title: A Watershed in a Pan: Parent Guide
endLine: Rain runs downhill and carries what it picks up downstream.

scenes.tts: Where does rain go after it lands on your street? It runs downhill. A paper landscape lets your child watch where it flows and collects.
scenes.caption: Where does rain go after it lands on your street? It runs downhill. A paper landscape lets your child watch where it flows and collects.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic street after rain: a puddle at the curb with a slow trickle running downhill toward a storm drain. Large high-contrast question text: 'Where does the rain go?' The trickle keeps moving. No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Where does rain go after it lands on your street? It runs downhill. A paper landscape lets your child watch where it flows and collects.

scenes.visual: The street sketch folds and crumples into a white paper landscape sitting in a baking tray. Title 'A Watershed in a Pan' appears above for two seconds.

scenes.tts: It takes about twenty-five minutes. Your child practices guessing where water will go and checking the guess. If you have a watershed map, you can also trace where rain from home drains.
scenes.caption: It takes about twenty-five minutes. Your child practices guessing where water will go and checking the guess. If you have a watershed map, you can also trace where rain from home drains.
scenes.visual: The crumpled paper in its tray stays at center-right. Three labels appear one by one with small icons: 'Guess, then check' (arrow), 'Look closely' (eye), 'Our watershed' (map pin).
scenes.narration: It takes about twenty-five minutes. Your child practices guessing where water will go and checking the guess. If you have a watershed map, you can also trace where rain from home drains.

scenes.tts: Gather white printer paper, washable markers, paper towels, and a shallow metal tray or plastic tub. Use plain water in a new spray bottle or one that has only held water. If you use a hole punch, handle it yourself.
scenes.caption: Gather white printer paper, washable markers, paper towels, and a shallow metal tray or plastic tub. Use plain water in a new spray bottle or one that has only held water. If you use a hole punch, handle it yourself.
scenes.visual: Items slide in around the tray: a sheet of paper, four washable markers (blue, brown, green, one other), a spray bottle labeled 'plain water only', paper towels, a small dish of cocoa, a few hole-punch dots. An old cleaner bottle fades in with a red X.
scenes.narration: Gather white printer paper, washable markers, paper towels, and a shallow metal tray or plastic tub. Use plain water in a new spray bottle or one that has only held water. If you use a hole punch, handle it yourself.

scenes.tts: Stay beside your child. Spray only at the paper, away from faces and pets. Keep paper dots and small marker caps away from children under four. Count the dots out and back in. If a child is choking, call nine one one.
scenes.caption: Stay beside your child. Spray only at the paper, away from faces and pets. Keep paper dots and small marker caps away from children under four. Count the dots out and back in. If a child is choking, call nine one one.
scenes.visual: Safety badges beside the tray, at most four: an adult near the table, a spray bottle aimed down at paper with a crossed-out face, a paper dot labeled 'Under 4: choking risk, call 911', and a tally '1, 2, 3' for counting dots.
scenes.narration: Stay beside your child. Spray only at the paper, away from faces and pets. Keep paper dots and small marker caps away from children under four. Count the dots out and back in. If a child is choking, call nine one one.

scenes.tts: Keep all supplies out of mouths. Cocoa is toxic to dogs and cats, so keep pets away. Wipe up cocoa and drips right away. Put cocoa-covered paper in a bin pets cannot open. Wash everyone's hands with soap and water when you finish.
scenes.caption: Keep all supplies out of mouths. Cocoa is toxic to dogs and cats, so keep pets away. Wipe up cocoa and drips right away. Put cocoa-covered paper in a bin pets cannot open. Wash everyone's hands with soap and water when you finish.
scenes.visual: Badges swap: a crossed-out mouth over a cocoa dish, a dog and cat with a 'keep away' sign, a towel wiping a floor drip, and soapy hands under a tap.
scenes.narration: Keep all supplies out of mouths. Cocoa is toxic to dogs and cats, so keep pets away. Wipe up cocoa and drips right away. Put cocoa-covered paper in a bin pets cannot open. Wash everyone's hands with soap and water when you finish.

scenes.tts: Crumple the paper into a tight ball. Open it gently, but don't flatten it. You want hills and valleys. Ask your child, 'Where is the highest ground?' Then trace each ridge in brown.
scenes.caption: Crumple the paper into a tight ball. Open it gently, but don't flatten it. You want hills and valleys. Ask your child, 'Where is the highest ground?' Then trace each ridge in brown.
scenes.visual: A sheet crumples into a ball, then opens into a hilly landscape in the tray. A finger traces along the ridge tops, and brown marker lines follow the finger. Label: 'ridge = high ground'.
scenes.narration: Crumple the paper into a tight ball. Open it gently, but don't flatten it. You want hills and valleys. Ask your child, 'Where is the highest ground?' Then trace each ridge in brown.

scenes.tts: Color one low corner blue and call it the bay. Tuck a folded towel under the other end, so the bay sits lowest. Then draw houses, a farm, and a road, some on hilltops and some in valleys.
scenes.caption: Color one low corner blue and call it the bay. Tuck a folded towel under the other end, so the bay sits lowest. Then draw houses, a farm, and a road, some on hilltops and some in valleys.
scenes.visual: One low corner fills with blue and is labeled 'the bay'. A folded towel slides under the far end and the tray tilts slightly toward the bay. Tiny green houses, a farm field and a road appear on hills and in valleys.
scenes.narration: Color one low corner blue and call it the bay. Tuck a folded towel under the other end, so the bay sits lowest. Then draw houses, a farm, and a road, some on hilltops and some in valleys.

scenes.tts: Now point to three spots, one on each side of a ridge and one by a house. Ask, 'If rain lands here, where will it go?' Your child draws a small arrow for each guess.
scenes.caption: Now point to three spots, one on each side of a ridge and one by a house. Ask, 'If rain lands here, where will it go?' Your child draws a small arrow for each guess.
scenes.visual: Three small dots appear: two on opposite sides of one ridge and one beside a house. Speech bubble: 'If rain lands here, where will it go?' Three small pencil arrows are drawn from the dots; they stay on screen.
scenes.narration: Now point to three spots, one on each side of a ridge and one by a house. Ask, 'If rain lands here, where will it go?' Your child draws a small arrow for each guess.

scenes.tts: Here is a question for you. Take two drops that land very close together, but on opposite sides of one ridge. Will they end up in the same place?
scenes.caption: Here is a question for you. Take two drops that land very close together, but on opposite sides of one ridge. Will they end up in the same place?
scenes.visual: Close-up of one ridge in the landscape. Two water drops hover just above it, one on each side. A high-contrast question card on the left: 'Same place, or not?'
scenes.narration: Here is a question for you. Take two drops that land very close together, but on opposite sides of one ridge. Will they end up in the same place?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and the two hovering drops; they bob very slightly. A soft ring turns beneath the question. No answer shown.

scenes.tts: Mist the paper from about a foot above, ten to twenty squirts. It can take several squirts before anything moves. Then the marker bleeds and runs down the creases. Drops on each side of a ridge go different ways.
scenes.caption: Mist the paper from about a foot above, ten to twenty squirts. It can take several squirts before anything moves. Then the marker bleeds and runs down the creases. Drops on each side of a ridge go different ways.
scenes.visual: A spray bottle mists from above, with a dashed line labeled 'about 1 foot'. After a pause, ink lines bleed and trickle down creases. The two drops from the question split: one runs down each side of the ridge into different valleys. Some color gathers in the blue bay.
scenes.narration: Mist the paper from about a foot above, ten to twenty squirts. It can take several squirts before anything moves. Then the marker bleeds and runs down the creases. Drops on each side of a ridge go different ways.

scenes.tts: Check the arrows together. Ask, 'Did the rain go where you guessed?' Then name it. All the land that drains to the same river or bay is one watershed. The ridges split one watershed from the next.
scenes.caption: Check the arrows together. Ask, 'Did the rain go where you guessed?' Then name it. All the land that drains to the same river or bay is one watershed. The ridges split one watershed from the next.
scenes.visual: The child's pencil arrows highlight one by one beside the real ink trails. Then soft color washes fill each drainage area, separated by the brown ridge lines, with the label 'watershed' on the one draining to the bay.
scenes.narration: Check the arrows together. Ask, 'Did the rain go where you guessed?' Then name it. All the land that drains to the same river or bay is one watershed. The ridges split one watershed from the next.

scenes.tts: A pinch of cocoa near the farm can stand in for fertilizer. If allergies or asthma rule out cocoa, use colored water with ingredients suitable for your child. You can skip both. Put a few paper dots on the road as litter. Spray again and watch where everything goes.
scenes.caption: A pinch of cocoa near the farm can stand in for fertilizer. If allergies or asthma rule out cocoa, use colored water with ingredients suitable for your child. You can skip both. Put a few paper dots on the road as litter. Spray again and watch where everything goes.
scenes.visual: Show either a pinch of cocoa or a few drops of colored water by the farm as pretend fertilizer. Show a few paper dots on the road as litter. Mist the paper. Follow the colored streak along a crease and show a paper dot shift slightly.
scenes.narration: A pinch of cocoa near the farm can stand in for fertilizer. If allergies or asthma rule out cocoa, use colored water with ingredients suitable for your child. You can skip both. Put a few paper dots on the road as litter. Spray again and watch where everything goes.

scenes.tts: If you have a map of Virginia's watersheds, find your town and follow the river to where it ends. Have your child pick three things your family can do and draw them. They could put trash in the bin or turn off the tap.
scenes.caption: If you have a map of Virginia's watersheds, find your town and follow the river to where it ends. Have your child pick three things your family can do and draw them. They could put trash in the bin or turn off the tap.
scenes.visual: A simple schematic map outline with a map pin on 'our town' and a river line traced to its end, marked 'schematic'. Three small icons appear for family actions: trash in the bin, a tree being planted, a tap turned off.
scenes.narration: If you have a map of Virginia's watersheds, find your town and follow the river to where it ends. Have your child pick three things your family can do and draw them. They could put trash in the bin or turn off the tap.

scenes.tts: Back on your street, rain can carry litter downhill into a storm drain. Your pan shows how water can pick things up and carry them downstream.
scenes.caption: Back on your street, rain can carry litter downhill into a storm drain. Your pan shows how water can pick things up and carry them downstream.
scenes.visual: Return to the opening street. Show a trickle carrying a small piece of litter into a storm drain. Follow one example route from the drain to a creek in a simple schematic.
scenes.narration: Back on your street, rain can carry litter downhill into a storm drain. Your pan shows how water can pick things up and carry them downstream.

scenes.line: Rain runs downhill and carries what it picks up downstream.
scenes.visual: End card with the wet paper landscape and its blue bay faint in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'Rain runs downhill and carries what it picks up downstream.'
